messages.subject: SE computation
parts:
Hello,
I am currently reading on Fisher Information and SE computation. My understanding is that SE for a laten trait can be computed doing the square root of the Test Information.
Trying on mirt I do not get the same result when extracting the SE from `fscores` and calculating it as square root of the test information extracted with testinfo.

Could you please explain why that is the case?

Thank you very mych,
Matteo Fiore

The code I ran

library(mirt)
library(stats4)
library(lattice)


data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
modfisher <- mirt(data, 1, '2PL', TOL=0.0001,SE=T, SE.type='Fisher')
mod <- mirt(data, 1, '2PL', TOL=0.0001,SE=T)
scoresfisher = fscores(modfisher, full.scores.SE=T)
scores = fscores(mod, full.scores.SE=T)
all(scores[,2] == scoresfisher[,2])
all(scores[,1] == scoresfisher[,1])


info = testinfo(mod, scores[,1])
se = 1./sqrt(info[100:110])
se
scores[100:110, ]
reversed_info = (1/scores[100:110,2])^2
reversed_info
info[100:110]

On Thu, Aug 1, 2019 at 5:04 AM Matteo Fiore <matteo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,
I am currently reading on Fisher Information and SE computation. My understanding is that SE for a laten trait can be computed doing the square root of the Test Information.
Trying on mirt I do not get the same result when extracting the SE from `fscores` and calculating it as square root of the test information extracted with testinfo.

This is only true when the SEs are obtained using maximum-likelihood estimation. Try passing method = 'ML' to fscores() and comparing to the results from testinfo. Currenlty, you're computing the posterior standard deviation for the EAP estimates, so these SEs/PDs will be more narrow than the ML results. HTH.

messages.subject: Re: SE computation
parts:
Thanks for the clarification, I have tried out and works as expected.
I did some additional research, and even though I do not understand in details yet why the information for 3PL is not equivalent to the second derivative of the log likelihood, I have tried to replicate the result found with the 2PL and ML estimation for 3PL.

I found out that there is a small difference between the Information calculated with testinfo and the one obtained with the following (the source is the book called 'Educational Measurements'):


1) Could you please explain the reason why?

2) Also, could you also explain why the testinfo function returns a different value from the inverse of the cube of the SE obtained from fscore?

3) Finally, could you please confirm that the formula used for SE computation in EAP is formula [5] from Bock, R. D., & Mislevy, R. J. (1982). Adaptive EAP estimation of ability in a microcomputer environment. Applied Psychological Measurement, 6, 431-444 ?


Thank you in advance.


Here is the code I ran

library(mirt)
library(stats4)
library(lattice)

model <- 'F = 1-5
          PRIOR = (5, g, norm, -1.5, 3)'

info_3PL <- function(a, c, prob) {
  Q <- 1-prob
  P <- prob
  res <- a ^ 2 * Q / P * ((P-c)/(1-c))^2
  return(res)
}

info_2PL <- function(a, prob) {
  Q <- 1-prob
  P <- prob
  res <- a^2*P*Q
  return(res)
}

prob_2PL <- function(a,d,theta){
  res <- 1/(1+ exp(-a*(theta+d)))
  return(res)
}

prob_3PL <- function(a,d,c,theta){
  res = c + (1-c) * prob_2PL(a,d,theta)
  return(res)
}

derivative_3PL <- function(a,d,c,theta){
   num <- a^2 * (c-1) * exp(a*theta + d) * ( exp(2*(a*theta+d)) - c ) 
   den <- (exp(a*theta + d) + 1)^2 * (exp(a*theta + d) + c)^2
   res = -1 * num / den
   return(res)
}


data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
modfisher3PL <- mirt(data, model, '3PL', TOL=0.0001,SE=T)
scoresfisher3PL = fscores(modfisher3PL, full.scores.SE=T, method='ML')

params3PL = coef(modfisher3PL)

info3PL = testinfo(modfisher3PL, scoresfisher3PL[,1])
se3PL = 1./sqrt(info3PL[400])
print(paste('se using 1/sqrt', se3PL))
print(paste('se using testinfo', scoresfisher3PL[400, 2]))
# SE calculated with 1/sqrt is lower than SE returned from fscores
# That means that the info from testinfo is higher than the one used in ML
reversed_info3PL = (1/scoresfisher3PL[400,2])^2
print(paste('info from (1/SE)^2', reversed_info3PL))
print(paste('info from testinfo', info3PL[400]))


# For item 2, let's check the second derivative against 
# the FI calculated with testinfo and against the FI calculated with formula
item2_fi_3PL <- testinfo(modfisher3PL, scoresfisher3PL[,1][400], which.items = 2)
prob_400_student_3PL <- prob_3PL(
  params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'], 
  params3PL$Item.2['par','d'], 
  params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], 
  scoresfisher3PL[,1][400]
)
fi_3PL <- info_3PL(params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'],params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], prob_400_student_3PL)

der <- derivative_3PL(params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'], 
                      params3PL$Item.2['par','d'], 
                      params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], 
                      scoresfisher3PL[,1][400])

print(paste('info with testinfo for item 2',item2_fi_3PL))
print(paste('info with formula for item 2', fi_3PL))
print(paste('derivative log likelihood for item 2', der))


# Check test info for student number 400
sum <- 0
for (x in seq(length(params3PL) - 1)){
  item <- params3PL[x]
  prob_400_student_3PL <- prob_3PL(
    item$Item['par','a1'], 
    item$Item['par','d'], 
    item$Item['par','g'], 
    scoresfisher3PL[,1][400]
  )
  sum <- sum + info_3PL(item$Item['par','a1'], item$Item['par','g'], prob_400_student_3PL)
}
print(paste('total info from sum of single items', sum))
print(paste('total info from testinfo', info3PL[400]))


and this is the output

"se using 1/sqrt 0.907764702691057"
"se using testinfo 0.783693193463438"

"info from (1/SE)^2 1.6282003745264"
"info from testinfo 1.2135381017704"

"info with testinfo for item 2 0.468410744959533"
"info with formula for item 2 0.483226340182395"
"derivative log likelihood for item 2 0.207689166659429"

"total info from sum of single items 1.0001032925286"
 "total info from testinfo 1.2135381017704"




Matteo Fiore

parts:
The reason this occurs is related to the observed versus expected information. For the 3PLM, observed != expected, but for the 2PLM and 1PLM this is the case. You can see Baker & Kim's (2004) book on the derivation of the 3PLM expected information (David Magis has written about this a few times as well).

Phil

parts: Thank you for the clarifications! I have run some more test and read some more papers and understood the problem.
On Tuesday, August 6, 2019 at 5:43:03 PM UTC+2, Phil Chalmers wrote:

The reason this occurs is related to the observed versus expected information. For the 3PLM, observed != expected, but for the 2PLM and 1PLM this is the case. You can see Baker & Kim's (2004) book on the derivation of the 3PLM expected information (David Magis has written about this a few times as well).

Phil
On Mon, Aug 5, 2019 at 9:19 AM Matteo Fiore <matteo...@gmail.com> wrote:

Thanks for the clarification, I have tried out and works as expected.
I did some additional research, and even though I do not understand in details yet why the information for 3PL is not equivalent to the second derivative of the log likelihood, I have tried to replicate the result found with the 2PL and ML estimation for 3PL.

I found out that there is a small difference between the Information calculated with testinfo and the one obtained with the following (the source is the book called 'Educational Measurements'):


1) Could you please explain the reason why?

2) Also, could you also explain why the testinfo function returns a different value from the inverse of the cube of the SE obtained from fscore?

3) Finally, could you please confirm that the formula used for SE computation in EAP is formula [5] from Bock, R. D., & Mislevy, R. J. (1982). Adaptive EAP estimation of ability in a microcomputer environment. Applied Psychological Measurement, 6, 431-444 ?


Thank you in advance.


Here is the code I ran

library(mirt)
library(stats4)
library(lattice)

model <- 'F = 1-5
          PRIOR = (5, g, norm, -1.5, 3)'

info_3PL <- function(a, c, prob) {
  Q <- 1-prob
  P <- prob
  res <- a ^ 2 * Q / P * ((P-c)/(1-c))^2
  return(res)
}

info_2PL <- function(a, prob) {
  Q <- 1-prob
  P <- prob
  res <- a^2*P*Q
  return(res)
}

prob_2PL <- function(a,d,theta){
  res <- 1/(1+ exp(-a*(theta+d)))
  return(res)
}

prob_3PL <- function(a,d,c,theta){
  res = c + (1-c) * prob_2PL(a,d,theta)
  return(res)
}

derivative_3PL <- function(a,d,c,theta){
   num <- a^2 * (c-1) * exp(a*theta + d) * ( exp(2*(a*theta+d)) - c ) 
   den <- (exp(a*theta + d) + 1)^2 * (exp(a*theta + d) + c)^2
   res = -1 * num / den
   return(res)
}


data <- expand.table(LSAT7)
modfisher3PL <- mirt(data, model, '3PL', TOL=0.0001,SE=T)
scoresfisher3PL = fscores(modfisher3PL, full.scores.SE=T, method='ML')

params3PL = coef(modfisher3PL)

info3PL = testinfo(modfisher3PL, scoresfisher3PL[,1])
se3PL = 1./sqrt(info3PL[400])
print(paste('se using 1/sqrt', se3PL))
print(paste('se using testinfo', scoresfisher3PL[400, 2]))
# SE calculated with 1/sqrt is lower than SE returned from fscores
# That means that the info from testinfo is higher than the one used in ML
reversed_info3PL = (1/scoresfisher3PL[400,2])^2
print(paste('info from (1/SE)^2', reversed_info3PL))
print(paste('info from testinfo', info3PL[400]))


# For item 2, let's check the second derivative against 
# the FI calculated with testinfo and against the FI calculated with formula
item2_fi_3PL <- testinfo(modfisher3PL, scoresfisher3PL[,1][400], which.items = 2)
prob_400_student_3PL <- prob_3PL(
  params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'], 
  params3PL$Item.2['par','d'], 
  params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], 
  scoresfisher3PL[,1][400]
)
fi_3PL <- info_3PL(params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'],params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], prob_400_student_3PL)

der <- derivative_3PL(params3PL$Item.2['par','a1'], 
                      params3PL$Item.2['par','d'], 
                      params3PL$Item.2['par','g'], 
                      scoresfisher3PL[,1][400])

print(paste('info with testinfo for item 2',item2_fi_3PL))
print(paste('info with formula for item 2', fi_3PL))
print(paste('derivative log likelihood for item 2', der))


# Check test info for student number 400
sum <- 0
for (x in seq(length(params3PL) - 1)){
  item <- params3PL[x]
  prob_400_student_3PL <- prob_3PL(
    item$Item['par','a1'], 
    item$Item['par','d'], 
    item$Item['par','g'], 
    scoresfisher3PL[,1][400]
  )
  sum <- sum + info_3PL(item$Item['par','a1'], item$Item['par','g'], prob_400_student_3PL)
}
print(paste('total info from sum of single items', sum))
print(paste('total info from testinfo', info3PL[400]))

Hello,
I am currently reading on Fisher Information and SE computation. My understanding is that SE for a laten trait can be computed doing the square root of the Test Information.

This is only true when the SEs are obtained using maximum-likelihood estimation. Try passing method = 'ML' to fscores() and comparing to the results from testinfo. Currenlty, you're computing the posterior standard deviation for the EAP estimates, so these SEs/PDs will be more narrow than the ML results. HTH.

Phil
